audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers read Darius, Darius, Skill, Darius, Skill, Darius, Darius. The Darius-side mirror is already set to Gnar, Darius, Darius, Darius, Darius, Darius, Skill, so four stages contradict it. Level 1 also contradicted this page's own whys[0], which says Gnar wins that trade outright.
audit.why: Apprehend (26/23.5/21/18.5/16s) does not exist at 1, so Mini's ranged autos beat a Decimate whose damage lives on the outer blade; from 3 the pull owns every all-in; at 2+ items the fight value swings back toward Gnar, which is why the mirror calls it Skill rather than either side.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Gnar, Darius, Darius, Darius, Darius, Darius, Skill on both layers, matching the mirror exactly.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page tracks Apprehend as the matchup-defining cooldown but never states its length, and level 6 was framed as a Gnar-neutral coinflip.
audit.why: Apprehend is 26s at rank 1 — the longest cooldown either side holds in lane and by far the biggest free window a Gnar gets. At 6 Darius gains Noxian Guillotine (120/100/80s) scaling with Hemorrhage stacks while Gnar gains no new spell, since GNAR! arrives with the Mega transform.
audit.corrected: 26s written into the cooldown block, the do's and the interactions report; level 6 rewritten as Darius's stage with the reason.

audit.whatIsWrong: Noxian Guillotine's true damage was never mentioned, while the itemization line recommends Plated Steelcaps — a reader could conclude armour answers his execute. The five-stack enrage was named in a don't's title with unrelated boilerplate underneath.
audit.why: Guillotine deals true damage increased per Hemorrhage stack and refreshes on a kill; armour and MR do nothing against it. Hemorrhage at five stacks also enrages him for a large AD gain.
audit.corrected: True damage and the five-stack enrage stated in itemization, the don'ts and the interactions report.

edits.before: Boomerang + hop kite wins every melee matchup early. Identify how Darius contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Mini's ranged autos plus a Boomerang win level 1 outright — Decimate only hurts on the outer blade and cannot tag you kiting.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Darius must walk into your range.
edits.after: Apprehend is up at 3: one pull drags Mini into Hemorrhage range and outer-blade Decimate heals through your poke.

edits.before: Mega + R against a wall is the best engage top lane owns. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Darius's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: At 6 you gain no spell while five stacks make Noxian Guillotine lethal true damage — fight only with the Rage bar full.

edits.before: Level 6 hands you only Rage RNG — Mega up means a Wallop-into-wall kill, Mega down means you concede the window, so it's a coinflip.
edits.after: Level 6 hands you only Rage RNG while he gains Noxian Guillotine's true damage off five stacks — more often than not you concede it.

edits.before: You out-range and out-teamfight him late — wall-GNAR! and kiting reclaim the game his single-target E can't follow into a 5v5.
edits.after: You out-teamfight him with wall-GNAR! and kiting, but he still deletes you in any isolated sidelane 1v1 — it nets out even.

edits.before: - Darius Apprehend: matchup-defining — His all-in start. Stay out of range. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Darius Apprehend (26s at rank 1): matchup-defining — his all-in starts here, so hold outside 535 range and treat a whiffed pull as 26 free seconds. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: kill windows only.

edits.before: His all-in start. Stay out of range. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: His all-in start, 26s at rank 1. Only engage once it is down or baited.

edits.before: Darius wastes Apprehend (Pull) — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Apprehend whiffed — you now own the next 26 seconds of the lane.

edits.before: Getting caught at zero rage right after Mega ends — that 15-second window is when Gnars die.
edits.after: Five Hemorrhage stacks enrage him and feed Guillotine's true damage — reset first.

edits.before: Track Darius's Apprehend (Pull): His all-in start. Stay out of range. When it is down — Boomerang-W + R him.
edits.after: Apprehend (26s at rank 1) starts everything — hold outside 535. Five stacks make his R lethal true damage.

edits.before: Start Doran's Blade + pot. Core: Stridebreaker  (stick + waveclear), then Sterak's Gage; boots Plated Steelcaps. Anti-heal (Oblivion Orb / Executioner's) early — his healing fights your pattern.
edits.after: Start Doran's Blade + pot. Core: Stridebreaker, then Sterak's Gage; boots Plated Steelcaps. Anti-heal early for Decimate's heal — and armour does nothing against Guillotine's true damage.

notes: Chart flips are one atomic group across both layers and are copied from the Darius-side mirror, including level 6 and 2+ items where this page's whys leaned the other way; I rewrote those two whys so the prose now agrees with the side rather than contradicting it. Apprehend's 26s at rank 1 is the single most useful number missing from the page — a whiffed pull is the longest free window in the lane. Per the mirror's note I did not assert that GNAR! creates terrain; Riot's description only stuns enemies thrown into a wall. breakdown.wave and breakdown.trading still carry PDF-extraction run-ons on this entry (same defect seen on garen); not touched.
